statement.essentials: A total parotidectomy removes both the outer and the inner parts of the gland while the nerve is kept; in benign disease it is kept for tumours that reach the inner part.
statement.anatomy: Total parotidectomy removes the superficial and deep lobes with the facial nerve preserved. In benign disease it is usually kept for deep-lobe tumours that contact the nerve, dumbbell tumours beneath the nerve, tumours of the superficial lobe that extend into the deep lobe, and multiple tumours.
statement.clinical: Its main downsides are more temporary and permanent facial nerve palsy, Frey syndrome and contour deformity. It is indicated for malignant tumours.

limitations: A narrative review’s account of indications, not a measurement. In this atlas the delivery of the deep lobe from beneath the nerve is drawn schematically.
